newsitem.title: NIGER: Niger opposition protest seeks release of leaders.
newsitem.headline: Niger opposition protest seeks release of leaders.

text.p: Up to 3,000 opposition supporters turned out for a protest rally in Niger's capital Niamey on Saturday to demand the release of three of their leaders detained on allegations of threatening state security.

Witnesses said a police helicopter hovered over the meeting, which was organised by women's groups and held in a traditional sports arena but no security forces deployed at the venue itself and there were no incidents reported.
Police deployed in force by the national assembly building and the university.

Former president Mahamane Ousmane, former parliament speaker Mahamadou Issoufou and Tandja Mamadou, leader of the former single party, the National Movement for a Development Society (MNSD), were arrested after a turbulent January 11 protest.

The three are part of an eight-party opposition alliance which accuses President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara of rigging July presidential elections to legitimise his rule after toppling Mahamane in a January 1996 coup.
Mainassara's supporters won a majority in November parliamentary elections in the West African nation.
Witnesses say up to 100 people have been arrested nationwide following the banned January 11 march which security forces broke up with tear gas. Officials speak of 62 arrests.
The marchers sought greater access to state media.
Former colonial power France and the United States, which condemned Mainassara's election as fraudulent, have urged the release of the three opposition leaders.
Mainassara seized power saying he wanted to end political deadlock paralysing government of the impoverished nation.
